extraction.name: AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes
extraction.description: A unified database of 15 optical marker-based human motion capture datasets containing 346 subjects, 11,451 motions, and approximately 42 hours of recordings. Motion is represented using SMPL body model parameters, including body shape, pose, articulated hands, and DMPL soft-tissue dynamics, enabling reconstruction of fully rigged 3D human meshes.
extraction.creator: Naureen Mahmood; Nima Ghorbani; Nikolaus F. Troje; Gerard Pons-Moll; Michael J. Black
extraction.citeAs: Naureen Mahmood, Nima Ghorbani, Nikolaus F. Troje, Gerard Pons-Moll, and Michael J. Black. AMASS: Archive of Motion Capture as Surface Shapes. arXiv:1904.03278v1 [cs.CV], 5 April 2019.
extraction.isLiveDataset: The authors state that they will continuously incorporate additional motion capture data contributed by themselves and the community.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The authors aggregated 15 motion capture datasets. Publicly available datasets were downloaded from the internet; additional datasets were obtained privately or recorded by the authors, including Dancers, Transitions, BioMotionLab, and SSM. MoSh++ converted the marker recordings into a common body representation. For SSM, three subjects performed 30 motions recorded using an OptiTrack optical motion capture system synchronized with a 3dMD 4D body scanner. Subjects wore minimal clothing, and reflective markers were placed directly on their skin wherever possible.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis; Physical data collection; Direct measurement
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Motion capture markers can become occluded by the body during movement. Simultaneous occlusion of multiple markers on a body part can produce unreliable or implausible pose estimates. Some recordings have no hand markers.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Optical marker-based motion capture recordings from ACCAD, BioMotion, CMU, EKUT, Eyes Japan, HumanEva, KIT, MPI HDM05, MPI Limits, MPI MoSh, SFU, SSM, TCD Hand, TotalCapture, and Transitions. Source marker sets vary in size from 37 to 91 markers and use different body locations. SSM additionally contains synchronized high-resolution 3D body scans captured at 60 frames per second.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: When recordings contain no hand markers, hand poses are set to the average pose of the MANO model. For missing or occluded body markers, MoSh++ increases the pose-prior weight according to the number of missing markers to obtain more plausible pose estimates.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: MoSh++ maps heterogeneous marker recordings into a shared representation combining SMPL-H and DMPL. It estimates body shape, pose, hand articulation when hand markers are present, and soft-tissue dynamics directly from marker positions rather than retargeting source skeletons to fixed body proportions.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Reconstruction results were manually inspected for motion capture problems such as swapped and mislabeled markers. Problems were either corrected or held out. Model fitting includes temporal smoothness terms to reduce marker jitter and regularization to handle varying marker counts and occlusion.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Body shape, pose, hand pose, and soft-tissue parameters were generated automatically by fitting the body model to observed markers with MoSh++. Results were manually inspected, and swapped or mislabeled marker problems were corrected or held out.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: MoSh++; SMPL-H; DMPL; MANO; Chumpy for automatic differentiation and Powell's dogleg minimization.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to continuously expand AMASS with additional motion capture data contributed by themselves and the community, and to support community additions provided the captures can be similarly shared. No release schedule, versioning scheme, or deprecation policy is specified.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes subject-specific 3D body shape and human motion information. The SSM component includes synchronized 4D body scans of subjects wearing minimal clothing, with markers placed directly on skin wherever possible. Two SSM subjects were professional models who signed modeling contracts permitting release of their scan and motion capture data.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Source recordings can contain swapped, mislabeled, missing, or occluded markers. Hand articulation is estimated only when hand markers are available; otherwise hands use the average MANO pose. The authors lack ground-truth data for quantitative evaluation of hand articulation. Given sparse markers, allowing too many shape or dynamics components causes overfitting. MoSh++ is not real-time, and improved missing-marker handling and fully automatic marker labeling are identified as future work.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training human motion models; animation and visualization; generating synthetic training images and video for computer vision; and training models for motion capture denoising and automatic marker labeling. The dataset is made available to the research community. Users interested only in pose may ignore shape and soft-tissue parameters, and users may normalize bodies to a common shape using the SMPL shape space.
